understanding: Step 1/2 of incident video for OKO: when a deferred person/animal VLM event (_PendingVlmEvent in src/oko/pipeline/live.py) resolves at ready_at, persist an MP4 of the incident window (trigger→resolve) to runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4 and surface the path on bridge_output.incident_video_path. The encoder lives in a new src/oko/live/video.py using cv2.VideoWriter with the mp4v codec at fps=10. Acceptance is a pytest that drives a delayed event to resolution, then reads the MP4 back via cv2 and asserts >1 frame. This is a code+commit task, one concern, no regressions.
summary: Accumulate incident frames on each _PendingVlmEvent across its delay window, add encode_incident_video(frames, out_path, fps=10) in src/oko/live/video.py (mp4v, graceful no-op when cv2/numpy/frames unusable), write runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4 at resolve time, add an incident_video_path field to BridgeOutput and set it via model_copy. Cover with a unit test (encode→readback) and an integration test (delayed event resolves→file exists→readback>1 frame), guarded by importorskip so existing dict-image tests stay green.

decision_atoms.statement: Add `frames: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list, compare=False)` to the frozen _PendingVlmEvent and append `captured.image` to every still-pending event each loop iteration (including the trigger iteration), before _resolve_ready_vlm_events runs.
decision_atoms.reason: Captures the full trigger→resolve window with minimal change; frozen dataclass forbids rebinding the attribute but appending to the referenced list is allowed, so mutation works without unfreezing.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A mutable list on a frozen dataclass is slightly surprising; without compare=False, equality/hash semantics involve an unhashable list (list.remove still works via __eq__, but hash() would raise). compare=False keeps identity-based behavior clean.

decision_atoms.statement: Add `incident_video_path: str | None = None` as a real field on BridgeOutput rather than smuggling it through model_copy.
decision_atoms.reason: BridgeOutput uses model_config extra='forbid'; an unknown key via model_copy(update=...) is fragile/non-serializable. A declared optional field is the correct, validated, backward-compatible carrier.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Touches the domain model (slightly wider than 'just live.py'), but it is the only correct way to satisfy the 'place path in bridge_output' constraint without breaking the forbid policy.

decision_atoms.statement: encode_incident_video returns str|None and is a graceful no-op (returns None, writes nothing) when cv2/numpy are unavailable, when there are <1 usable ndarray frames, or when the VideoWriter fails to open (writer.isOpened()==False).
decision_atoms.reason: Existing pipeline tests feed dict images ({'frame': id}); a hard dependency on real arrays would regress them. None-on-failure mirrors the existing encode_frames_jpeg_b64 contract and keeps the pipeline crash-free.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Silent failure can hide a misconfiguration; mitigated by returning None (so incident_video_path simply stays unset) and by an explicit unit test on the happy path.

decision_atoms.statement: Wire video writing into the pending-resolve path only (_resolve_pending_vlm_event → _resolve_vlm_event), scoping Step 1 to deferred person/animal events.
decision_atoms.reason: Those events already own a frame buffer and a clear trigger→ready_at window; immediate events have no accumulated window. Keeps the change to 'Один концерн'.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Immediate (non-deferred) events get no video in this step; that is deliberately deferred to Step 2 and should be stated as a boundary, not an omission.

decision_atoms.statement: Add an injectable `incidents_dir: Path = Path('runs/incidents')` constructor param on LivePipeline; mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) lazily before writing; filename is `<sanitized event_id>.mp4`.
decision_atoms.reason: Default satisfies the literal runs/incidents/<event_id>.mp4 constraint while letting the integration test target tmp_path for isolation (no repo pollution, deterministic assertions).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: One extra constructor arg; negligible API surface and fully backward-compatible via the default.

decision_atoms.statement: Acceptance = two tests guarded by pytest.importorskip('cv2'): a unit test (N synthetic uint8 BGR ndarrays → encode → cv2.VideoCapture readback frame count >1) and an integration test (BufferingEventBuilder-style run with real ndarray captured.image, deferred event resolves → bridge_output.incident_video_path set → file exists under tmp incidents_dir → readback >1 frame).
decision_atoms.reason: Directly matches every success_test (delayed event, file at path, openable, >1 frame, no regressions) and isolates the encoder for fast failure localization.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Two tests instead of one add a little surface, but the unit test pinpoints encoder bugs the integration test would only report obscurely.

assumptions: cv2 (opencv) and numpy are installed in the runtime/test env — strongly indicated since src/oko/providers/camera.py uses cv2.VideoCapture and src/oko/vlm/frame_codec.py uses cv2.imencode; tests still guard with importorskip for safety.
Real camera frames are uint8 BGR numpy ndarrays of consistent (H, W); test/fake frames are plain dicts and must be tolerated as 'no video'.
event_id (built_event.event.event_id) is unique-enough and filesystem-safe after light sanitization to use as the MP4 filename.
The mp4v fourcc is available on the target OS (Windows 11) for VideoWriter; if the writer fails to open, encode returns None and the path stays unset.
The incident window (person_animal_vlm_delay_seconds ≈ 3.5s) is short, so buffering raw frames per pending event is memory-bounded and acceptable.
It is acceptable to add one optional field to BridgeOutput (domain change) to honor the bridge_output.incident_video_path constraint under extra='forbid'.

risks.risk: extra='forbid' on BridgeOutput rejects/garbles incident_video_path if injected only via model_copy without declaring the field.
risks.mitigation: Declare incident_video_path: str | None = None on the model; set it through model_copy(update=...) which then targets a real, serializable field.

risks.risk: cv2.VideoWriter with mp4v silently fails to open (missing codec/backend), producing a 0-byte or unreadable file.
risks.mitigation: Check writer.isOpened() before writing; return None on failure; assert file existence AND cv2.VideoCapture readback frame count >1 in the test so a broken writer fails loudly in CI.

risks.risk: Adding a mutable list to a frozen dataclass breaks hashing/equality assumptions used by list.remove during resolution.
risks.mitigation: Mark frames with field(compare=False) so equality stays based on stable identifying fields; never hash _PendingVlmEvent (it is only stored in/removed from a list).

risks.risk: Existing tests feed dict images; a real-array assumption in the encoder or unconditional file write would regress them.
risks.mitigation: Encoder filters non-ndarray/None frames and no-ops to None; pipeline only sets incident_video_path when a path is returned, so dict-image runs are unaffected.

risks.risk: Writing into the repo's real runs/incidents during tests pollutes the working tree and makes assertions flaky.
risks.mitigation: Inject incidents_dir=tmp_path in tests; keep the default of runs/incidents only for production.

risks.risk: Mixed frame sizes or grayscale frames in the buffer cause VideoWriter to drop/garble frames.
risks.mitigation: Minimal: derive size from the first frame and skip mismatched frames. Advanced: resize to the first frame's size and convert grayscale→BGR.

minimal_version: 1) src/oko/live/video.py: encode_incident_video(frames, out_path, fps=10) -> str|None — drop None/non-ndarray frames; if <1 remain or cv2/numpy missing return None; size from first frame; fourcc=cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*'mp4v'); mkdir parents; if not writer.isOpened() return None; write same-size frames, skip mismatches; release; return str(out_path). 2) src/oko/pipeline/live.py: add frames list (compare=False) to _PendingVlmEvent; in run() append captured.image to each still-pending event each iteration before resolving; add incidents_dir param (default Path('runs/incidents')); on _resolve_pending_vlm_event compute incidents_dir/'<event_id>.mp4', call encoder, and if path returned set bridge_output via model_copy(update={'incident_video_path': path}). 3) src/oko/domain/bridge.py: add incident_video_path: str | None = None. 4) tests/test_incident_video.py: unit encode→readback>1 frame, and integration delayed-event-resolves→file exists→readback>1 frame, both importorskip('cv2') and using tmp_path. Run pytest; commit as a single focused change.
advanced_version: All of minimal, plus: resize/convert frames to the first frame's (H, W) and BGR so heterogeneous buffers still encode; expose fps and codec via OkoConfig instead of hardcoding; emit incident_video_path only after fsync/size>0 verification and add structured logging on writer-open failure; thread the path into evidence_references as well; add a tiny CLI/reporter hook to point at the saved clip; parametrize the test across frame counts and a grayscale case; and stub Step 2 (immediate-event video + retention/cleanup of runs/incidents) behind a clear TODO without implementing it here.
